newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak crown strengthens on Czech c.bank moves.
newsitem.headline: Slovak crown strengthens on Czech c.bank moves.

text.p: The Slovak crown strengthened in early trading on Thursday with dealers saying the appreciation was linked to intervention by the Czech National Bank (CNB) to support the Czech crown earlier in the day.
The Slovak crown opened at around -0.40 percent versus the mark/dollar parity but it strengthened to some 30 basis points below the midpoint in the first two hours of trade.

"We are very closely linked to the Czech crown, foreigners are playing the two crowns (Slovak and Czech) together," said Dusan Svitek, a trader at the largest Slovak forex market player, Slovenska Sporitelna.

The CNB on Thursday morning twice directly intervened on the market to support the crown and helped it stabilise at less than four percent below parity, after it had touched levels near minus 5.0 percent.
Svitek said he expected the Slovak crown to find some resistance at around -0.1 percent against its parity.
"It will much depened on what happens on the Czech market - if the Czech crown gets stronger we will go along with its trend," he said.
Tibor Fratrik, a dealer at ING Bank, said he saw the crown moving within a range of -0.25 to -0.45 percent versus the basket midpoint during the day.
"Money market rates have gone down today, making the interest rate differential less attractive, so there should not be too big a demand for Slovak crowns," Fratrik said.

The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Thursday offered 6.0 billion crowns in its refinancing repo tender, a sum that should help the banking sector meet the miminum reserves requirement at the Thursday deadline.
In a reaction to the NBS repo tender, o/n rates fell to around 25 percent on Thursday, down from around 32 percent on Wednesday.
